##  · K5-q-minimum — R12: 'current minimum' when the queue is empty, and whether the running budget counts

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Evidence: Clarifies R12's 'current minimum' in service of the WP-K5 acceptance line 'a sleeping-waking budget cannot exceed its share': the lowest pass among runnable budgets including the running one (as last charged), floored by a monotone virtual time held across idle. Wake pass = max(own, floor). Also: wrap-safe on both widths; new budgets enter at the floor; a one-line R12 clarification in the K5 docs commit; model mutation R12NoFloorWhenIdle; an idle-gap boot case. The owner confirms at plan approval.

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `83e606bfbf220fe7a0f8493eb913f88f` · 2026-09-24T17:52:34Z

> R12 says "on wake, pass = max(own pass, current minimum)". Two cases are unspecified.
> 
> (1) No other budget is runnable at the wake instant, i.e. the system is idle. The model then keeps the waker's own pass. Attack: A sleeps with a low pass while B runs alone, and B's pass climbs. B blocks briefly, the system idles, and A wakes (timed with rdtime). A keeps its stale low pass, so when B wakes at max(B, A) A runs until it catches up. A has banked credit while asleep, which RESOURCES says a waking budget cannot do. The model's fairness generator always keeps a spinner runnable, so it never sees this.
> 
> (2) Does the minimum include the running budget (at its pass as last charged)?
> 
> Recommendation: current minimum = the lowest pass among runnable budgets, including the running one, floored by a monotone virtual-time value. The floor is raised to that minimum whenever it changes, and kept when the queue empties, so wake pass = max(own, floor). That is the standard stride global pass. It changes no weights or shares, only closes the idle-gap bank. The model gets the same rule and a mutation, R12NoFloorWhenIdle, caught by a new idle-gap property.
> 
> Ask: approve the definition, or state another.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `8bceee145541c1390ba67f62fde8c4f5` · 2026-09-24T17:53:23Z

> Approved as you define it. It's a clarification of "current minimum" that serves R12's intent and the WP-K5 line "a sleeping-waking budget cannot exceed its share", not a new rule.
> - current minimum = the lowest pass among runnable budgets, including the running one at its pass as last charged. It's floored by a monotone virtual-time value that rises to that minimum whenever the minimum changes and holds when the queue empties. Wake pass = max(own, floor).
> - The floor uses the same width and wrap-safe comparison as passes, on rv32 and rv64. Cover it in the plan's overflow section.
> - A new budget, or a thread's first run, enters at the floor too, unless the spec already says otherwise. Check it and say so in the plan.
> - Add a one-line R12 clarification (next to the I13 one) in the K5 docs commit. Model: the same rule, plus the mutation R12NoFloorWhenIdle, caught by the idle-gap property. Add a boot case for the idle-gap attack as you describe it (A sleeps, B runs alone, idle gap, A wakes), so the kernel is tested and not only the model.
> The owner sees this at plan approval.
